selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit reverts loop-idiom support for hoisting loop memcpy operations to a loop preheader. It removes the generic memory-intrinsic processing helper and the memcpy-specific recognition path, leaving runOnLoopBlock to scan and transform only loop memset instructions through the prior iterator-recovery logic.
Changed symbols: LoopIdiomRecognize::runOnLoopBlock; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemIntrinsic; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemCpy; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad
Behavioral change: Stops recognizing loop memcpy intrinsics as candidates for promotion/hoisting to a larger preheader memcpy.; Removes the memcpy path that computes affine source and destination SCEVs, checks matching strides, and calls processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad.; Restores explicit block iteration that only processes MemSetInst operations in runOnLoopBlock.; Removes memcpy-specific optimization remarks introduced with the hoisting feature.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 optimizer-produced invalid-IR failure.; No matching source reproducer or dominance-specific regression test is shown in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopIdiomRecognize; LLVM scalar optimizer; loop preheader hoisting; ScalarEvolution; DominatorTree
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate because it explicitly disables a transformation that hoists a loop memcpy to the preheader. Such a move can expose a use before its defining instruction when source, destination, or dependent values are not available on all paths to the preheader—the exact class of condition reported by the verifier. The retrieved code also shows that the removed path uses loop SCEVs and calls a shared load/store transformation routine. This commit is a revert, so its direct behavior is to eliminate the risky transformation rather than introduce it; nevertheless, that is evidence that the reverted memcpy-hoisting feature is a credible source of the invalid IR.
Causal confidence: 0.72
Build risk: Removes both the declaration and definition of the generic processLoopMemIntrinsic helper, reducing dangling-reference risk in the shown code.; The retrieved hunks contain no new or updated regression test for the reverted memcpy-hoisting behavior.; The change narrows optimization coverage by disabling loop memcpy hoisting while retaining loop memset processing.

top_candidates.subject: [MemCpyOpt] Allow variable lengths in memcpy optimizer
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This MemCpyOpt change broadens selected memcpy optimizations to accept equal variable-length operands rather than requiring both lengths to be constants. It also adjusts undefined-content and memcpy-to-memset eligibility checks, and adds coverage for variable-sized memcpy/memset cases under both MemorySSA and non-MemorySSA modes.
Changed symbols: MemCpyOptPass::processMemCpyMemCpyDependence; MemCpyOptPass::processMemCpy; hasUndefContentsMSSA; MemCpyOptPass::performMemCpyToMemSetOptzn
Behavioral change: Permits memcpy-to-memcpy dependence folding when the two length operands are the same SSA Value, including non-constant lengths; unequal lengths still require comparable ConstantInt lengths.; Uses the memcpy's actual length in the undefined-content check instead of the local CopySize value.; Changes memcpy-to-memset gating so the memcpy size, rather than the source memset size, must be a known constant.; Removes one shown MemorySSA must-alias/constant-length early-success condition from undefined-content recognition.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces during -O1 optimization after invalid IR is produced.; The added tests exercise variable-sized memory intrinsics and verify MemorySSA, but do not test a dominance failure or the reported C reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: MemCpyOpt; LLVM scalar optimizer; MemorySSA
Causal explanation: The commit changes an optimizer that can delete, replace, or redirect memory-intrinsic operations, so it is within the broad -O1 optimizer risk area. However, the retrieved changes are length/equivalence and undef-content eligibility checks; they show no CFG restructuring, SSA value motion, PHI rewriting, or explicit dominance maintenance. The tests validate variable-size memory behavior and MemorySSA rather than the reported verifier domination condition. Thus the link is plausible but indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.24
Build risk: Adds three focused MemCpyOpt IR tests.; Tests run with both -enable-memcpyopt-memoryssa=0 and =1; the latter additionally uses -verify-memoryssa.; No direct verifier or dominance regression test is present in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit is another retrieved revert of the loop memcpy preheader-hoisting work, with the same visible substantive effect as 2bd4049: it removes generic MemCpyInst processing from Loop Idiom Recognize, restores the memset-only block scan, and returns processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad to its StoreInst/LoadInst-specific implementation and alignment handling.
Changed symbols: LoopIdiomRecognize::runOnLoopBlock; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad(StoreInst *, const SCEV *); LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad(Value *, Value *, unsigned, MaybeAlign, MaybeAlign, Instruction *, Instruction *, const SCEVAddRecExpr *, const SCEVAddRecExpr *, const SCEV *); processLoopMemIntrinsic<MemCpyInst>; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemCpy; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemSet
Behavioral change: Removes generic loop processing of MemCpyInst and retains only the explicit MemSetInst recognition loop.; Deletes the generalized processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad entry point that accepts separate pointers, MaybeAlign values, and generic instructions.; Restores store/load-specific atomic checks, alignment checks, and CreateMemCpy inputs using SI and LI.; Removes the visible newly introduced route for hoisting loop memcpy intrinsics into a preheader.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 invalid-IR verifier failure.; This revert disables the preceding scalar loop memcpy-hoisting behavior that may place a new instruction before definitions used by it.; The retrieved hunks provide no direct PR50585 testcase result, no verifier output from this revision, and no pass trace naming loop-idiom.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopIdiomRecognize.cpp; Loop Idiom Recognize; scalar loop optimization
Causal explanation: The visible patch removes the same preheader-memcpy transformation route that is relevant to domination preservation. Therefore it is more plausibly a mitigation for a possible invalid-IR bug than an introducing change. top_candidates.subject: [Verifier] Fail on overrunning and invalid indices for {insert,extract} vector intrinsics
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends `Verifier::visitIntrinsicCall` to reject invalid `llvm.experimental.vector.insert` and `llvm.experimental.vector.extract` calls. It obtains the constant index and vector element counts, requires indices to be multiples of the inserted/extracted vector's known minimum length, and—when the source and sub/result vector have matching scalable-ness—rejects operations whose selected range overruns the parent vector. New verifier tests cover invalid alignment and overrun cases for fixed and scalable vectors while deliberately allowing mixed scalable-parent/fixed-subvector cases that cannot be statically size-compared.
Changed symbols: Verifier::visitIntrinsicCall; Intrinsic::experimental_vector_insert; Intrinsic::experimental_vector_extract; extract_idx_not_constant_multiple; insert_idx_not_constant_multiple; extract_overrun_fixed_fixed; insert_overrun_fixed_fixed
Behavioral change: Adds verifier assertions that insert/extract indices are constant multiples of the relevant subvector/result known-minimum element count.; Adds bounds checks for fixed/fixed and scalable/scalable vector insertions and extractions.; Changes malformed experimental vector insert/extract IR from potentially being accepted to producing verifier diagnostics.; Does not rewrite optimizer output, repair dominance, or modify CFG/value placement.
Assertion or trace link: Direct subsystem match: the failure is reported while the verifier is running.; No added diagnostic matches the reported dominance failure: the new messages concern invalid vector-intrinsic indices and vector overruns, not `Instruction does not dominate all uses` or `Broken function found`.
Reproducer link: The added tests are hand-written invalid `llvm.experimental.vector.{insert,extract}` calls.; No retrieved test connects these intrinsics to the compact C `-O1` reproducer or to a non-dominating instruction use.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM IR Verifier; Experimental vector insert/extract intrinsic validation
Causal explanation: The commit directly touches the verifier pass named by the crash signal, so it could change whether certain malformed IR is rejected. However, it only strengthens validation of vector-intrinsic index and bounds rules; it neither produces IR nor changes the verifier's dominance checking. The displayed evidence therefore does not support it as the cause of the reported optimizer-created dominance violation.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Previously accepted malformed experimental vector insert/extract IR will now fail verification.; New tests use exact verifier diagnostic text, making diagnostic wording part of test compatibility.; No pr50585-specific or dominance-verifier regression test is present in the retrieved hunks.

selected_hunks.patch:
diff --git a/llvm/test/Verifier/insert-extract-intrinsics-invalid.ll b/llvm/test/Verifier/insert-extract-intrinsics-invalid.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e7bf59085713
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Verifier/insert-extract-intrinsics-invalid.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+; RUN: not opt -verify -S < %s 2>&1 >/dev/null | FileCheck %s
+
+;
+; Test that extractions/insertion indices are validated.
+;
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract index must be a constant multiple of the result type's known minimum vector length.
+define <4 x i32> @extract_idx_not_constant_multiple(<8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <4 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v4i32.v8i32(<8 x i32> %vec, i64 1)
+  ret <4 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_insert index must be a constant multiple of the subvector's known minimum vector length.
+define <8 x i32> @insert_idx_not_constant_multiple(<8 x i32> %vec, <4 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.v8i32.v4i32(<8 x i32> %vec, <4 x i32> %subvec, i64 2)
+  ret <8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+;
+; Test that extractions/insertions which 'overrun' are captured.
+;
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract would overrun.
+define <3 x i32> @extract_overrun_fixed_fixed(<8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v8i32.v3i32(<8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract would overrun.
+define <vscale x 3 x i32> @extract_overrun_scalable_scalable(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <vscale x 3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <vscale x 3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; We cannot statically check whether or not an extraction of a fixed vector
+; from a scalable vector would overrun, because we can't compare the sizes of
+; the two. Therefore, this function should not raise verifier errors.
+; CHECK-NOT: experimental_vector_extract
+define <3 x i32> @extract_overrun_scalable_fixed(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.v3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: subvector operand of experimental_vector_insert would overrun the vector being inserted into.
+define <8 x i32> @insert_overrun_fixed_fixed(<8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.v8i32.v3i32(<8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec, i64 6)
+  ret <8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: subvector operand of experimental_vector_insert would overrun the vector being inserted into.
+define <vscale x 8 x i32> @insert_overrun_scalable_scalable(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <vscale x 3 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <vscale x 8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <vscale x 3 x i32> %subvec, i64 6)
+  ret <vscale x 8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; We cannot statically check whether or not an insertion of a fixed vector into
+; a scalable vector would overrun, because we can't compare the sizes of the
+; two. Therefore, this function should not raise verifier errors.
+; CHECK-NOT: experimental_vector_insert
+define <vscale x 8 x i32> @insert_overrun_scalable_fixed(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <vscale x 8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.nxv8i32.v3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec, i64 6)
+  ret <vscale x 8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+declare <vscale x 3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32>, i64)
+declare <vscale x 8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32>, <vscale x 3 x i32>, i64)
+declare <vscale x 8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.nxv8i32.v3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32>, <3 x i32>, i64)
+declare <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.v3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32>, i64)
+declare <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v8i32.v3i32(<8 x i32>, i64)
+declare <4 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v4i32.v8i32(<8 x i32>, i64)
+declare <8 x i32> @llvm.ex

top_candidates.subject: [LoopUnroll] Eliminate PreserveCondBr parameter and fix a bug in the process
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes LoopUnroll control-flow handling in llvm::UnrollLoop while eliminating the PreserveCondBr-based model. It distinguishes complete unrolling from exact unrolling, computes an exact trip count for the specific exiting branch when available, retains runtime-trip-count/peeling exclusion, and updates regression expectations so unrolled/peeled loops preserve conditional exit branches instead of assuming an upper-bound trip count permits removal of loop-control checks.
Changed symbols: llvm::UnrollLoop; llvm::simplifyLoopAfterUnroll; UnrollLoopOptions; ScalarEvolution::getSmallConstantTripCount; pr45939-peel-count-and-complete-unroll.ll; test1
Behavioral change: Introduces CompletelyUnroll based on ULO.Count == ULO.TripCount, while separately recognizing ExactUnroll from the exiting branch's exact constant trip count.; Removes PreserveCondBr documentation and changes the stated TripCount contract from a latch-specific exit bound to a general upper bound on header executions.; Keeps conditional loop-control branches when an upper-bound-based unroll is not proven exact; updated tests expect branches such as br i1 true to retained loop-body/exit targets rather than unconditional removal of the exit structure.; Continues to reject the combination of runtime trip-count unrolling and peeling with an assertion.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found
Reproducer link: -O1 compilation abort after an optimizer produces invalid IR; Loop-unroll regression test explicitly covers peeling and complete-unroll control-flow behavior
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LoopUnroll.cpp; LoopUnroll; ScalarEvolution trip-count reasoning; CFG and SSA/LCSSA-sensitive loop transformation
Causal explanation: This is the strongest visible candidate because it changes an optimizer utility that clones/rewires loop CFGs and depends on trip-count and exiting-branch reasoning. Incorrectly eliminating or retaining a latch/exiting conditional branch during unrolling can alter predecessor sets, PHI inputs, and the placement/reachability of cloned definitions, all of which are relevant to verifier dominance failures. The tests specifically demonstrate changed exit-edge behavior. However, the retrieved evidence does not name pr50585, include its testcase, show the reported domination diagnostic, or prove that LoopUnroll runs on this reproducer at -O1; the link is therefore plausible but not direct.

@@ -362,0 +342,15 @@ LoopUnrollResult llvm::UnrollLoop(Loop *L, UnrollLoopOptions ULO, LoopInfo *LI,
+  // Are we eliminating the loop control altogether?  Note that we can know
+  // we're eliminating the backedge without knowing exactly which iteration
+  // of the unrolled body exits.
+  const bool CompletelyUnroll = ULO.Count == ULO.TripCount;
+
+  // We assume a run-time trip count if the compiler cannot
+  // figure out the loop trip count and the unroll-runtime
+  // flag is specified.
+  bool RuntimeTripCount =
+      (ULO.TripCount == 0 && ULO.Count > 0 && ULO.AllowRuntime);
+
+  assert((!RuntimeTripCount || !ULO.PeelCount) &&
+         "Did not expect runtime trip-count unrolling "
+         "and peeling for the same loop");

index 5f7395d4cbec..fa0a51424a8a 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LoopUnroll.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LoopUnroll.cpp
@@ -248,12 +248,3 @@ void llvm::simplifyLoopAfterUnroll(Loop *L, bool SimplifyIVs, LoopInfo *LI,
-/// TripCount is the upper bound of the iteration on which control exits
-/// LatchBlock. Control may exit the loop prior to TripCount iterations either
-/// via an early branch in other loop block or via LatchBlock terminator. This
-/// is relaxed from the general definition of trip count which is the number of
-/// times the loop header executes. Note that UnrollLoop assumes that the loop
-/// counter test is in LatchBlock in order to remove unnecesssary instances of
-/// the test.  If control can exit the loop from the LatchBlock's terminator
-/// prior to TripCount iterations, flag PreserveCondBr needs to be set.
-///
-/// PreserveCondBr indicates whether the conditional branch of the LatchBlock
-/// needs to be preserved.  It is needed when we use trip count upper bound to
-/// fully unroll the loop.
+/// TripCount is an upper bound on the number of times the loop header runs.
+/// Note that the trip count does not need to be exact, it can be any upper
+/// bound on the true trip count.

steps.subject: [SimplifyCFG] Fix SimplifyBranchOnICmpChain to be undef/poison safe.

evidence: Directly modifies SimplifyCFG, an -O1 CFG-rewriting scalar transform that creates branch and switch control flow.
It inserts a newly created freeze before a rewritten branch and enables a formerly suppressed transformation path, making SSA placement relevant even though the documented bug is poison safety.
features: branch-condition-rewrite, cfg-rewrite, freeze-insertion, meta:core-llvm, o1-scalar-optimizer, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes SimplifyCFG's ICmp-chain branch simplification so that an ExtraCase value that is not proven non-undef/non-poison is frozen before it is made eagerly evaluated by the transformed control flow. It also removes the previous MemorySanitizer-only bailout, allowing the transform under MSan while preserving poison/undef safety. The accompanying SimplifyCFG tests now expect a freeze before the rewritten branch and the resulting switch-based path.
Changed symbols: SimplifyCFGOpt::SimplifyBranchOnICmpChain; test_no_msan; test_msan; test7
Behavioral change: Removes the hasFnAttribute(Attribute::SanitizeMemory) guard that previously disabled the ExtraCase transformation under MemorySanitizer.; Queries isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison(ExtraCase, Options.AC, BI, nullptr) and inserts Builder.CreateFreeze(ExtraCase) when the value may be undef or poison.; Changes generated SimplifyCFG output so the branch condition may be a newly inserted freeze, followed by the switch.early.test CFG path.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses (issue diagnostic only; not present in the retrieved hunk)
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces during clang -O1 compilation.; The retrieved tests exercise SimplifyCFG directly with opt and include poison/undef branch-condition cases, but do not reproduce the reported verifier failure.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/SimplifyCFG.cpp; CFG and SSA-producing scalar transformation
Causal explanation: This is a real implementation change in a CFG-rewriting optimizer utility. Introducing a freeze and enabling a previously suppressed CFG rewrite can affect value placement and branch uses, which is generally relevant to verifier-sensitive dominance failures. However, the stated and tested defect is eager evaluation of undef/poison, not use of a non-dominating instruction; no retrieved hunk touches the verifier or demonstrates the pr50585 reproducer, assertion, or an invalid SSA edge.
Causal confidence: 0.23
Build risk: Implementation change uses AssumptionCache through Options.AC and adds IRBuilder freeze creation in an existing transformation path.; Regression coverage was updated for both normal and sanitize_memory functions and for existing switch-creation tests.; No direct crash-anchor contact or verifier-specific regression test is present in the retrieved evidence.

+    // There can be an unintended UB if extra values are Poison. Before the

+    // condition, and it will not raise UB. But after transformation, we are
+    // evaluating extra values before checking the condition, and it will raise
+    // UB. It can be solved by adding freeze instruction to extra values.
+    AssumptionCache *AC = Options.AC;

+    if (!isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison(ExtraCase, AC, BI, nullptr))

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes SimplifyCFG's ICmp-chain branch simplification so that an ExtraCase value that is not proven non-undef/non-poison is frozen before it is made eagerly evaluated by the transformed control flow. It also removes the previous MemorySanitizer-only bailout, allowing the transform under MSan while preserving poison/undef safety. The accompanying SimplifyCFG tests now expect a freeze before the rewritten branch and the resulting switch-based path.
Changed symbols: SimplifyCFGOpt::SimplifyBranchOnICmpChain; test_no_msan; test_msan; test7
Behavioral change: Removes the hasFnAttribute(Attribute::SanitizeMemory) guard that previously disabled the ExtraCase transformation under MemorySanitizer.; Queries isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison(ExtraCase, Options.AC, BI, nullptr) and inserts Builder.CreateFreeze(ExtraCase) when the value may be undef or poison.; Changes generated SimplifyCFG output so the branch condition may be a newly inserted freeze, followed by the switch.early.test CFG path.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses (issue diagnostic only; not present in the retrieved hunk)
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces during clang -O1 compilation.; The retrieved tests exercise SimplifyCFG directly with opt and include poison/undef branch-condition cases, but do not reproduce the reported verifier failure.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/SimplifyCFG.cpp; CFG and SSA-producing scalar transformation
Causal explanation: This is a real implementation change in a CFG-rewriting optimizer utility. Introducing a freeze and enabling a previously suppressed CFG rewrite can affect value placement and branch uses, which is generally relevant to verifier-sensitive dominance failures. However, the stated and tested defect is eager evaluation of undef/poison, not use of a non-dominating instruction; no retrieved hunk touches the verifier or demonstrates the pr50585 reproducer, assertion, or an invalid SSA edge.
Causal confidence: 0.23
Build risk: Implementation change uses AssumptionCache through Options.AC and adds IRBuilder freeze creation in an existing transformation path.; Regression coverage was updated for both normal and sanitize_memory functions and for existing switch-creation tests.; No direct crash-anchor contact or verifier-specific regression test is present in the retrieved evidence.

+    // There can be an unintended UB if extra values are Poison. Before the
+    // transformation, extra values may not be evaluated according to the

+    AssumptionCache *AC = Options.AC;

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved test changes reflect an X86 SLP masked-gather profitability change. In delete_pointer_bound, the expected SLP output changes from constructing a vector of pointers and issuing llvm.masked.gather.v2f32.v2p0f32 to two scalar GEPs, two scalar loads, and insertelement assembly of the <8 x float> argument. Associated tests split AVX512F and AVX512VL check prefixes, while LoopVectorize gather/scatter expectations remove an unrolled vector-loop shape. The retrieved material does not include the CostModel or vectorizer implementation hunk responsible for these expected-output updates.
Changed symbols: delete_pointer_bound; test_gather_not_profitable_pr48429; SLPVectorizer; LoopVectorize; llvm.masked.gather.v2f32.v2p0f32
Behavioral change: The delete_pointer_bound test now expects masked gather formation to be rejected or no longer selected for the shown loads.; Expected output is scalarized into b+10 and b+14 GEPs, scalar loads, and insertelement operations instead of a vector pointer construction, masked gather, and shuffle chain.; AVX512F and AVX512VL expectations are separated in PR47629 test RUN lines.; The visible LoopVectorize test expectation removes a vector-loop unrolling setup and expects a simpler vector.ph/vector.body phi structure.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; llvm::report_fatal_error; llvm::FPPassManager::runOnFunction
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 clang failure after invalid IR is produced.; No retrieved hunk refers to PR50585, 'Instruction does not dominate all uses', 'Broken function found', or the original C testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; X86 CostModel; LoopVectorize test coverage

The shown delete_pointer_bound function does contain separate then/else blocks, but the changed expected values are produced and consumed within the else block, while the then block independently uses b.14. Nothing in the retrieved function context indicates a value is moved across a non-dominating control-flow edge. Without the production implementation hunk, there is no evidence of a dominance-breaking transformation.

top_candidates.subject: [CostModel][X86] Adjust sext/zext SSE/AVX legalized costs based on llvm-mca reports.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved changes are test-only adjustments associated with revised X86 legalized sext/zext costs. CostModel tests split SSE2 and SSE4.1 expectations and revise several numeric costs. SLPVectorizer tests change the expected output for small integer extensions: for SSE2, the tests now expect separate scalar loads, scalar sext/zext operations, and insertelement construction rather than a vector load plus vector extension; SLM retains the vector-load/vector-extension expectation in the visible sext cases. No retrieved production hunk shows the cost-model implementation or an IR transformation implementation.
Changed symbols: add; umul; loadext_2i8_to_2i64; loadext_4i16_to_4i64; SLPVectorizer; X86 CostModel
Behavioral change: CostModel test expectations change for legalized X86 sext/zext operations, including separate SSE2 and SSE4.1 cost baselines.; For loadext_2i8_to_2i64 under SSE2, the expected SLP result changes from a vector load and vector sext/zext to scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement assembly.; The corresponding poison tests expect the same scalarized construction rooted at poison rather than undef.; The visible SLM expectations preserve vector load/vector-extension output for the same small-extension pattern.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; llvm::report_fatal_error; llvm::FPPassManager::runOnFunction
Reproducer link: The reported failure occurs during clang -O1 -w -c.; No retrieved hunk includes the PR50585 reproducer or an expected verifier diagnostic.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 CostModel; SLPVectorizer
Causal explanation: This candidate has a plausible indirect connection because revised cost decisions can cause SLP to choose scalar assembly instead of vectorized extension sequences, changing optimizer-generated IR. The visible scalar assembly is a straight-line sequence of loads, extensions, and insertelements, with no CFG edits or cross-block use shown. Since no implementation hunk establishes a faulty insertion/replacement path and no verifier/dominance test is added, the evidence is insufficient to tie this commit to PR50585's domination failure.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Retrieved hunks are tests only; no direct production build breakage is evidenced.; Changes affect cost-model numeric baselines and SLPVectorizer output baselines across SSE2, SSE4.1, SLM, and AVX-oriented configurations.; The poison and undef variants increase test sensitivity to IR-construction semantics, but they do not themselves demonstrate invalid IR.; Crash-aware metadata reports zero touched crash files.

steps.subject: [AArch64] Cost-model i8 vector loads/stores

evidence: Changes executable AArch64 TTI memory costs and enables additional SLP/LoopVectorize output.
It is target-specific profitability logic rather than a producer-side dominance or CFG-preservation change.
features: aarch64-tti, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Target/AArch64, path:llvm/test/Analysis/CostModel, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64TargetTransformInfo memory-operation costing for extending loads and truncating stores whose scalar element sizes differ. In AArch64TTIImpl::getMemoryOpCost, v4i8 is now assigned cost 2 because it lowers to a scalar load/store plus sshll/xtn, while other affected vectors receive a scalarization cost of two operations per element. The associated SLP and LoopVectorize tests are updated to expect profitable <4 x i8> vectorization, including replacement of four scalar byte load/compute/store chains with a <4 x i8> load, vector arithmetic, and a vector store.
Changed symbols: AArch64TTIImpl::getMemoryOpCost; f_noalias; test_load_i8_store_i32; test_load_i32_store_i8; SLPVectorizer AArch64 loadi8 test checks; LoopVectorize AArch64 extend-vectorization-factor-for-unprofitable-memops test checks
Behavioral change: AArch64 cost modeling now treats v4i8 extending loads/truncating stores as profitable enough to cost two instructions rather than using the removed special profitability calculation.; Other mismatched-scalar-size vector memory operations are explicitly modeled as scalarized at two operations per vector element.; SLPVectorizer and LoopVectorize can consequently select <4 x i8> vectorization in cases previously expected to remain scalar or require a larger vectorization factor.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; llvm::report_fatal_error; llvm::FPPassManager::runOnFunction
Reproducer link: The issue occurs during clang -O1 and reports an Instruction does not dominate all uses verifier failure.; The updated tests show optimizer-generated vector IR for AArch64 byte load/store and extension/truncation workloads, but do not run the supplied reproducer or check verifier validity.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 TargetTransformInfo; SLPVectorizer; LoopVectorize
Causal explanation: This is the strongest of the three candidates because it changes executable profitability logic that can enable additional vectorizer rewrites, and the test diffs confirm that vectorized IR is newly selected. Nevertheless, getMemoryOpCost itself only supplies costs; it does not rewrite instructions or maintain dominator state. The shown generated IR is a single entry block with producer-before-user ordering, and no CFG/dominance-sensitive transformation is visible. Absent evidence that the failing target is AArch64 or that an enabled vectorization path produces the invalid cross-block use, the causal link remains weak.
Causal confidence: 0.10
Build risk: Production implementation is changed, but it is target-specific AArch64 TTI costing rather than verifier or dominance infrastructure.; Tests validate changed vectorization decisions for SLPVectorizer and LoopVectorize, increasing optimizer-path coverage.; No visible test invokes clang -O1 with verifier checking or asserts preservation of dominance after the newly profitable vectorization.

define void @test_load_i8_store_i32(i8* noalias %src, i32* noalias %dst, i32 %off, i64 %N) {
; CHECK-LABEL: @test_load_i8_store_i32(

entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.next, %loop ], [ 0, %entry ]
  %gep.src = getelementptr inbounds i8, i8* %src, i64 %iv
  %lv = load i8, i8* %gep.src, align 1
  %lv.ext = zext i8 %lv to i32
  %add = add i32 %lv.ext, %off
  %gep.dst = getelementptr inbounds i32, i32* %dst, i64 %iv
  store i32 %add, i32* %gep.dst
  %iv.next = add nuw nsw i64 %iv, 1
  %exitcond.not = icmp eq i64 %iv.next, %N
  br i1 %exitcond.not, label %exit, label %loop

exit:

}

In AArch64TTIImpl::getMemoryOpCost, v4i8 is now assigned cost 2 because it lowers to a scalar load/store plus sshll/xtn, while other affected vectors receive a scalarization cost of two operations per element. The associated SLP and LoopVectorize tests are updated to expect profitable <4 x i8> vectorization, including replacement of four scalar byte load/compute/store chains with a <4 x i8> load, vector arithmetic, and a vector store.

Summary: The visible first-parent changes update X86 SLPVectorizer test expectations for SSE-legalized integer/float conversions. Besides normalizing FileCheck option syntax, the tests now expect vectorized SSE sequences for mixed sitofp/uitofp cases and for groups of i16-to-float conversions, replacing prior scalar extract/load/convert/insert-element sequences. The retrieved material does not include the production CostModel or SLPVectorizer implementation responsible for those expected-output changes.
Changed symbols: sitofp_uitofp_4i32_8i16_16i8; sitofp_16i16_16f32; uitofp_16i16_16f32; SLPVectorizer X86 sitofp test RUN directives; SLPVectorizer X86 alternate-cast test checks
Behavioral change: SLPVectorizer test expectations change from scalar i8/i16 conversion and insertion sequences to vector shuffles, vector sitofp/uitofp operations, and vector result assembly under SSE.; The tests also distinguish SSE and SLM expected output rather than using one shared CHECK expectation.; This is evidence that a cost-model-related change changes vectorization profitability/selection, but the implementation-level change is not visible in the retrieved hunks.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; llvm::report_fatal_error; llvm::FPPassManager::runOnFunction
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 clang failure caused by invalid IR with an Instruction does not dominate all uses verifier diagnostic.; The visible tests exercise opt -slp-vectorizer, including poison-based insertelement/shufflevector test inputs, but do not show the issue reproducer, -O1 pipeline execution, or a verifier failure.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; X86 conversion cost modeling
Causal explanation: The changed expected SLP output establishes a plausible indirect route: altered conversion costs can make SLP choose vectorized rewrites that were previously rejected. However, the visible output is straight-line dataflow composed of conversions and shufflevectors, with no CFG edge, PHI update, instruction motion across blocks, or replacement operation that could explain a dominance violation. The implementation that changes profitability is unavailable here, so the evidence supports only weak subsystem proximity, not causation.

top_candidates.subject: [CostModel][X86] Adjust sext/zext SSE/AVX legalized costs based on llvm-mca reports.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved hunks update X86 CostModel and SLPVectorizer tests for legalized sext/zext costs. In the shown SLP expectations, SSE2 changes from vector loads and vector extensions to scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement reconstruction for narrow-to-i64 extensions, while SLM/AVX expectations retain vectorized forms. The retrieved evidence nevertheless consists only of tests; it does not show the implementation responsible for changing cost decisions.
Changed symbols: loadext_2i8_to_2i64; loadext_4i16_to_4i64; llvm/test/Analysis/CostModel/X86/cast.ll; llvm/test/Analysis/CostModel/X86/intrinsic-cost-kinds.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer/X86/sext.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer/X86/zext.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer/X86/sext-inseltpoison.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer/X86/zext-inseltpoison.ll
Behavioral change: Changes expected X86 CostModel estimates for legalized sext/zext operations, including distinct SSE2 and SSE4.1 expectations.; Changes the expected SSE2 SLP result for loadext_2i8_to_2i64 from a vector load plus vector sext/zext to scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement assembly.; Retains vectorized extension expectations for the shown SLM and AVX cases, indicating target-dependent vectorization profitability changes.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 clang verifier failure involving a non-dominating instruction.; The retrieved test functions exercise SLP vectorization of extension loads, including poison-based vector construction, but do not reproduce the reported verifier error.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 CostModel; SLPVectorizer
Causal explanation: The shown expected behavior changes whether SLP forms vector extension operations or leaves/reconstructs them scalarly, which can alter optimizer output and therefore is more plausibly adjacent to an optimizer-verifier bug than a pure test-only formatting change. Still, no retrieved production hunk establishes that the cost change itself performs unsafe value replacement or CFG manipulation, and the shown transformations are straight-line load/extend/insertelement sequences rather than dominance-sensitive CFG rewrites.
Causal confidence: 0.15
Build risk: Retrieved evidence is test-only; the implementation of the revised X86 legalization costs is not available in the hunks.; Tests cover both undef and poison insertelement forms, which provides some IR-validity-sensitive coverage, but not dominance verification.; No retrieved test invokes the clang -O1 pipeline or checks the issue's verifier diagnostic.

Still, no retrieved production hunk establishes that the cost change itself performs unsafe value replacement or CFG manipulation, and the shown transformations are straight-line load/extend/insertelement sequences rather than dominance-sensitive CFG rewrites.

build_risk: Retrieved evidence is test-only; the implementation of the revised X86 legalization costs is not available in the hunks.
Tests cover both undef and poison insertelement forms, which provides some IR-validity-sensitive coverage, but not dominance verification.
No retrieved test invokes the clang -O1 pipeline or checks the issue's verifier diagnostic.

Summary: The retrieved LoopVectorize test updates describe a CFG simplification in vectorized-loop epilog handling: middle.block now branches unconditionally to scalar.ph when the scalar loop must execute, and exit/LCSSA PHIs no longer carry middle.block incoming values. The resulting tested IR routes the vector resume value through scalar.ph and removes obsolete vector-middle values such as IND_ESCAPE1 and VECTOR_RECUR_EXTRACT_FOR_PHI from downstream exit PHIs. No production LoopVectorize hunk is retrieved, but the expected IR directly documents the intended CFG and PHI-invariant change.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor][FIX] Do not replace a value with a non-dominating instruction
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Attributor fix prevents replacement with an instruction that does not dominate the replacement use. The retrieved regressions split expected results by old/new pass managers and preserve calls or PHI-based values in cases where aggressive interprocedural constant propagation previously simplified through CFG joins. A newly added ctx_test case has a value defined only in a conditional predecessor and consumed through a PHI in the join block, directly exercising dominance-sensitive value simplification.
Changed symbols: Attributor value-replacement logic; ctx_test; fn_no_null_opt; fn2; fn0; fn1; PR26044.ll; PR16052.ll
Behavioral change: Attributor replacement is constrained so that an instruction cannot substitute for a value at uses it does not dominate.; The ctx_test regression retains the branch-local call result through a PHI at the join before truncation, rather than permitting an invalid direct replacement across the conditional CFG.; Updated IPConstantProp expectations show that old-PM Attributor output may retain calls to fn0/fn1 instead of propagating their returned argument through callers, while new-PM expectations remain separately specified.
Assertion or trace link: Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found; Verifier; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: The reported failure is invalid optimized IR at -O1 followed by verifier failure.; The added ctx_test regression has the same essential shape: %i is defined only in the then block, reaches join through a PHI, and is consumed after the join. Replacing the PHI-derived value with %i at join would violate dominance on the entry-to-join path.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; interprocedural constant propagation; Attributor value simplification/replacement
Causal explanation: The commit subject names the precise verifier invariant implicated by pr50585, and the retrieved regression explicitly exercises a conditional definition, PHI merge, and later use—the canonical configuration for a non-dominating replacement. Although no implementation hunk or explicit pr50585 reproducer is included in the retrieved material, the semantic match to the reported diagnostic is direct and strong.
Causal confidence: 0.93
Build risk: Regression expectations are expanded to distinguish old-PM and new-PM Attributor behavior, increasing pipeline-specific test surface.; Tests cover both translation-unit and CGSCC modes and validate changed interprocedural constant-propagation output.; No verifier-source change or direct crash-stack file touch is shown; confidence comes from the dominance-specific fix and CFG regression.

Summary: The retrieved first-parent hunks update vectorizer regression-test expectations for an X86 masked-gather cost-model change. In particular, SLP output for delete_pointer_bound is now expected to remain scalar rather than form a masked gather, and several AVX512-specific check-prefix names and LoopVectorize expected CFG/details are adjusted. No implementation hunk is available here, so the precise source-level cost-model logic cannot be attributed beyond the commit subject and changed tests.
Changed symbols: SLPVectorizer masked-gather cost model; delete_pointer_bound; test_gather_not_profitable_pr48429; AVX512F; AVX512VL
Behavioral change: The SLP test expectation for delete_pointer_bound changes from constructing vector pointers and issuing llvm.masked.gather to scalar GEPs, scalar loads, and insertelement operations.; AVX512F and AVX512VL runs are split into distinct FileCheck prefixes.; LoopVectorize gather/scatter test expectations remove an unrolled vector-loop setup and instead expect a simpler vector-loop PHI structure; this is test-observable output only in the retrieved evidence.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found
Reproducer link: The reported failure occurs under clang -O1 and is an invalid-IR dominance failure.; The retrieved changes concern X86 vectorizer output and masked-gather profitability, not the reported compact C reproducer or a verifier failure.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; LoopVectorize; X86 vectorization cost modeling
Causal explanation: Vectorization rewrites can in principle create or replace values across CFG regions and therefore are verifier-sensitive. The causal link is therefore weak.

top_candidates.subject: [CostModel][X86] Adjust sext/zext SSE/AVX legalized costs based on llvm-mca reports.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved hunks are test-only updates accompanying adjusted X86 sext/zext legalized-cost expectations. The SLPVectorizer checks for loadext_2i8_to_2i64 change the expected SSE2 result from a vector load plus vector extension into two scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement reconstruction, while other target checks retain vectorized forms. CostModel expectations are also split or revised for SSE2/SSE4.1 and for one overflow intrinsic cost. No retrieved hunk modifies the SLPVectorizer, CostModel implementation, verifier, or dominance utilities.
Changed symbols: loadext_2i8_to_2i64; loadext_4i16_to_4i64; add; umul; X86 SLPVectorizer sext/zext FileCheck checks; X86 CostModel FileCheck checks
Behavioral change: Updates expected X86 CostModel estimates for legalized sext/zext operations and one vector overflow intrinsic.; Updates expected SSE2 SLP output for narrow-load widening cases from vector extension to scalar loads/extensions followed by insertelement construction.; The visible evidence demonstrates changed optimization selection expectations, not a production change that moves instructions across basic blocks or rewrites use-def dominance.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; llvm::report_fatal_error
Reproducer link: The failure occurs under Clang -O1 and reports invalid IR through the verifier.; Retrieved tests invoke the SLP vectorizer and validate cast/vectorization output, but contain no reproducer, verifier invocation, or domination diagnostic matching pr50585.
Pass or subsystem link: X86 CostModel; SLPVectorizer
Causal explanation: The candidate is more relevant than a pure analysis-only change because the updated SLP expectations show that cost decisions can choose scalar reconstruction instead of vectorized extension on SSE2. Such profitability decisions could change optimization paths. Still, the retrieved hunks contain no evidence of an invalid-IR-producing rewrite, CFG edit, PHI update, or failed dominance preservation, so the link to the exact verifier failure remains indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: All retrieved hunks are tests; the production implementation responsible for the cost adjustments is not present in the retrieved evidence.; The selected evidence omits 190 hunks, preventing attribution of any unshown implementation behavior.; Visible risk is primarily changed test expectations across X86 subtargets and possible target-specific output-baseline changes.

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RET:%.*]] = trunc i64 [[PHI]] to i32

+;

+  br label %join

+  %ret = trunc i64 %phi to i32
+  ret i32 %ret

Summary: This is an Attributor dominance-preservation fix, as stated directly by the subject. The retrieved tests add a control-flow-sensitive @ctx_test case where a value `%i` is defined only in `then` and reaches `join` through a phi, and revise IP constant-propagation expectations so that some pipelines retain calls to @fn0/@fn1 rather than folding their results indiscriminately. The checks preserve the phi-based value flow and distinguish old/new pass-manager behavior.
Changed symbols: AAValueSimplify/value replacement logic (identified by commit subject; implementation hunk not retrieved); @test; @ctx_test; @fn0; @fn1; @fn2; @fn_no_null_opt; Attributor IPConstantProp regression checks
Behavioral change: Prevents replacing a value with an instruction that does not dominate every replaced use, per the commit subject.; Adds a branch-and-join regression case in @ctx_test: `%i` is created in `then`, incorporated through `%phi` in `join`, and then truncated for the return value.; Updates IPConstantProp expectations so OPM configurations retain calls such as `call i32 @fn1(i32 %tmp0)` or `call i32 @fn0(i32 %tmp0)` and return propagated arguments from @fn0/@fn1, instead of relying on the prior `ret ... undef` expectations.
Assertion or trace link: Instruction does not dominate all uses; verifier; Broken function found; non-dominating instruction
Reproducer link: The added @ctx_test test has a definition in a conditional `then` block and a join-block phi, directly exercising the class of CFG-sensitive replacement for which a non-dominating replacement would violate IR dominance.; The retrieved tests do not include the exact PR50585 C source or its -O1 command line.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AAValueSimplify/value replacement; IPConstantProp; LLVM IR dominance invariant
Causal explanation: The candidate's stated fix exactly matches the reported verifier failure: replacing a use with an instruction that does not dominate that use produces `Instruction does not dominate all uses`. The newly added conditional-definition/phi regression is concrete dominance-sensitive test evidence. Although the implementation hunk itself was not retrieved and the exact PR50585 source is absent, this is a direct, mechanism-level match to the issue.
Causal confidence: 0.94
Build risk: The candidate changes Attributor/IPConstantProp expected output across legacy/new PM and CGSCC configurations.; Only test hunks are visible; 34 omitted hunks likely contain the implementation-side dominance guard.; The new regression coverage is explicitly CFG and value-replacement sensitive, so it is high relevance to verifier-validity testing.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/Attributor/value-simplify.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/Attributor/value-simplify.ll
index 1d23a20890c4..78575c343dba 100644
--- a/llvm/test/Transforms/Attributor/value-simplify.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/Attributor/value-simplify.ll
@@ -1226,0 +1227,41 @@ define internal i1 @cmp_null_after_cast(i32 %a, i8 %b) {
+
+declare i8* @m()
+
+define i32 @test(i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define {{[^@]+}}@test
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[R:%.*]] = call i32 @ctx_test(i1 [[C]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[R]]
+;
+  %r = call i32 @ctx_test(i1 %c)
+  ret i32 %r
+}
+
+define internal i32 @ctx_test(i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define {{[^@]+}}@ctx_test
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label [[THEN:%.*]], label [[JOIN:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[M:%.*]] = tail call i8* @m()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = ptrtoint i8* [[M]] to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[JOIN]]
+; CHECK:       join:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[I]], [[THEN]] ], [ undef, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RET:%.*]] = trunc i64 [[PHI]] to i32
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[RET]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %c, label %then, label %join
+
+then:
+  %m = tail call i8* @m()
+  %i = ptrtoint i8* %m to i64
+  br label %join
+
+join:
+  %phi = phi i64 [ %i, %then ], [ undef, %entry ]
+  %ret = trunc i64 %phi to i32
+  ret i32 %ret
+}
+

The connection is therefore plausible but weakly evidenced.

The retrieved regression tests add a branch/phi case in `ctx_test` where a value defined only in the `then` block flows through a `join` phi, and revise Attributor IPConstantProp expectations so optimized outputs retain calls and returned-argument behavior rather than applying the prior replacement/simplification patterns. The visible evidence is primarily tests, but it precisely targets the invalid-IR class reported by pr50585.

top_candidates.subject: [OpenMP] Detect SPMD compatible kernels and execute them as such
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds OpenMPOpt support for recognizing target kernels as SPMD-compatible and manifesting that decision by changing the kernel execution-mode global and the arguments of OpenMP target initialization/deinitialization calls. The change also records incompatible runtime calls, emits optimization remarks explaining either generic-mode fallback or SPMD conversion, and adds NVPTX OpenMP regression coverage.
Changed symbols: AAKernelInfoFunction::changeToSPMDMode; AAKernelInfoCallSite; SPMDCompatibilityTracker; NumOpenMPTargetRegionKernelsSPMD; A.changeUseAfterManifest
Behavioral change: For kernels whose SPMDCompatibilityTracker is assumed compatible, changes the `<kernel>_exec_mode` global initializer from 1 to 0.; Rewrites the relevant __kmpc_target_init arguments to request SPMD mode and disable the generic runtime state machine, and rewrites __kmpc_target_deinit to indicate SPMD mode.; Keeps kernels in generic mode when tracked instructions or unknown OpenMP runtime calls are incompatible, emitting analysis remarks for the blocking instructions.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error; Instruction does not dominate all uses
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 compilation of a compact C testcase producing invalid IR.; The retrieved tests exercise OpenMP target kernels on nvptx64 rather than the reported generic compact-C reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/OpenMPOpt.cpp; OpenMP target-kernel optimization; Attributor manifest-time use rewriting
Causal explanation: This is an optimizer change that rewrites IR operands during Attributor manifestation, so it is verifier-relevant in principle. However, the visible rewrites replace call operands with constants and mutate a global initializer; they do not visibly move instructions, replace CFG edges, or create a value use across a non-dominating path. The functionality is also specific to OpenMP target kernels and the added coverage uses NVPTX. The retrieved evidence therefore provides only a weak causal route to the reported dominance failure.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Implementation change is accompanied by OpenMPOpt IR tests and Clang OpenMP remark tests.; New coverage explicitly checks rewritten target-init/deinit arguments and execution-mode globals.; No Verifier.cpp, scalar optimizer, dominance-analysis, or generic CFG utility change is shown.

%0 = call i32 @__kmpc_target_init(%struct.ident_t* @1, i1 false, i1 true, i1 true)
  %exec_user_code = icmp eq i32 %0, -1
  br i1 %exec_user_code, label %user_code.entry, label %worker.exit

user_code.entry:                                  ; preds = %entry
  %1 = call i32 @__kmpc_global_thread_num(%struct.ident_t* @1)
  store i32 %1, i32* %.threadid_temp., align 4
  call void @__omp_outlined__(i32* %.threadid_temp., i32* %.zero.addr) #2
  call void @__kmpc_target_deinit(%struct.ident_t* @1, i1 false, i1 true)
  ret void

worker.exit:                                      ; preds = %entry
  ret void
}

; Verify we will not store a constant true here even though initially all call sites pass `i1 true` for  the second-to-last argument.
define internal i32 @__kmpc_target_init(%struct.ident_t*, i1, i1 %use_generic_state_machine, i1) {
  store i1 %use_generic_state_machine, i1* @V
  %call = call i32 @unknown()
  ret i32 %call
}

; Function Attrs: convergent norecurse nounwind
define internal void @__omp_outlined__(i32* noalias %.global_tid., i32* noalias %.bound_tid.) #0 {
entry:
  %.global_tid..addr = alloca i32*, align 8
  %.bound_tid..addr = alloca i32*, align 8
  store i32* %.global_tid., i32** %.global_tid..addr, align 8
  store i32* %.bound_tid., i32** %.bound_tid..addr, align 8
  call void @no_parallel_region_in_here() #8
  ret void
}

; Function Attrs: convergent nounwind
define hidden void @no_parallel_region_in_here() #1 {
entry:
  %0 = call i32 @__kmpc_global_thread_num(%struct.ident_t* @2)
  %1 = call i32 @__kmpc_single(%struct.ident_t* @2, i32 %0)
  %2 = icmp ne i32 %1, 0
  br i1 %2, label %omp_if.then, label %omp_if.end

omp_if.then:                                      ; preds = %entry
  store i32 0, i32* @G, align 4
  call void @__kmpc_end_single(%struct.ident_t* @2, i32 %0)
  br label %omp_if.end

omp_if.end:                                       ; preds = %omp_if.then, %entry
  call void @__kmpc_barrier(%struct.ident_t* @3, i32 %0)
  ret void
}

; Function Attrs: nounwind
declare i32 @__kmpc_global_thread_num(%struct.ident_t*) #2

declare void @__kmpc_target_deinit(%struct.ident_t*, i1, i1)

; The second to last argument of __kmpc_target_init is is set to false to indicate we do not need the generic runtime state machine.

Summary: An Attributor fix titled "Traverse uses even if a value is assumed constant." The retrieved hunks show corresponding test expectation changes for argument promotion and other Attributor analyses: the expected optimized form of run becomes unreachable in a CGSCC case, previous non-CGSCC call/argument-promotion expectations are restored, and multiple tests revise fixed-point iteration limits.
Changed symbols: run; CaptureAStruct; UseLongDoubleUnsafely; UseLongDoubleSafely; AccessPaddingOfStruct
Behavioral change: The visible fp80 test changes expected Attributor output for run, removing expectations for a promoted CaptureAStruct call in selected pipeline modes and expecting an unreachable body in the CGSCC result.; Attributor regression tests adjust maximum iteration counts in align.ll, nodelete.ll, internal-noalias.ll, memory_locations.ll, and ArgumentPromotion tests.; Per the commit subject, the intended analysis behavior is to continue traversing uses even after a value is assumed constant; the retrieved code does not show the implementation of that traversal.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: -O1 compilation aborts after invalid IR is produced
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; argument promotion; interprocedural optimization
Causal explanation: A change to use traversal under constant assumptions can affect what Attributor proves and subsequently manifests, including call and argument-promotion decisions. Such transformations are plausibly verifier-sensitive in the abstract. Still, only test hunks were retrieved; they provide no implementation-level evidence of a dominance-breaking value replacement, instruction move, CFG rewrite, or stale dominance analysis. The changed contexts do not match the reported verifier text, and nothing ties the compact -O1 reproducer to this Attributor path. Therefore this is a subsystem-level lead, not a demonstrated cause.

The visible safety checks cover reachability and transfer behavior but do not establish that all operands dominate the new predecessor location.
features: divrempairs, dominance-sensitive-cfg-rewrite, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/test/Transforms/DivRemPairs, ssa-instruction-hoisting
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends DivRemPairs::optimizeDivRem to hoist paired division/remainder operations from a triangular CFG into a common predecessor. It moves the division, and sometimes the remainder, before the predecessor terminator after reachability and guaranteed-transfer checks; where a native div-rem operation is unavailable, the hoisted division enables replacement of the remainder with multiplication and subtraction.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; DivRemPairsPass::run; DivRemPairsLegacyPass; remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges
Behavioral change: DivRemPairs now recognizes a RemBB -> DivBB triangular shape with a unique predecessor for RemBB and hoists DivInst into PredBB when all PredBB successors are DivBB or RemBB.; The new IsSafeToHoist check requires every instruction preceding the candidate div/rem in its original block to be guaranteed to transfer execution to its successor.; When a combined div-rem operation exists, both operations are moved to PredBB; otherwise the division is hoisted and the remainder can be decomposed into mul/sub using that division.; The tests verify that udiv and urem are hoisted to entry for i64 cases and that the i128 remainder becomes mul/sub using the hoisted division, with freeze operations added to preserve poison semantics.
Assertion or trace link: Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found; verifier; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 optimizer-produced invalid-IR failure detected by the verifier.; This pass performs the exact high-risk operation for such a failure: moving SSA-producing instructions across basic blocks and then introducing or retaining uses of those values.; The new regression cases are triangular CFGs in which div/rem values are moved from branch-specific blocks into their common predecessor.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/DivRemPairs.cpp; DivRemPairs scalar optimization; DominatorTree
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate because the hunk explicitly changes SSA instruction placement to establish dominance before reusing the division in the remainder computation. The visible guards validate control-flow reachability and whether execution reaches the original operations, but do not visibly validate that every operand of the moved DivInst or RemInst dominates PredBB. If an operand is defined only in one of the original blocks, moving the operation to PredBB would immediately create a non-dominating operand use and trigger the reported verifier diagnostic. The exact issue testcase and pass pipeline are not provided, so this remains an evidence-backed hypothesis rather than confirmation.
Causal confidence: 0.76
Build risk: The core implementation hunk and focused transform tests were retrieved; only 5 hunks were omitted.; The pass requests and preserves CFG analyses while moving instructions without changing CFG edges, which is consistent with the shown transformation but makes SSA/dominance preconditions especially important.; Regression tests check expected transformed IR, including negative may-throw coverage in visible context, but do not explicitly run the verifier or the reported clang -O1 testcase.; Crash-aware metadata reports text-unreachable because no crash-anchor contact was found; the causal evidence instead comes from the direct dominance-sensitive instruction movement.

causal_evidence.summary: This commit extends DivRemPairs::optimizeDivRem to hoist paired division/remainder operations from a triangular CFG into a common predecessor. It moves the division, and sometimes the remainder, before the predecessor terminator after reachability and guaranteed-transfer checks; where a native div-rem operation is unavailable, the hoisted division enables replacement of the remainder with multiplication and subtraction.
behavioral_change: DivRemPairs now recognizes a RemBB -> DivBB triangular shape with a unique predecessor for RemBB and hoists DivInst into PredBB when all PredBB successors are DivBB or RemBB.
The new IsSafeToHoist check requires every instruction preceding the candidate div/rem in its original block to be guaranteed to transfer execution to its successor.
When a combined div-rem operation exists, both operations are moved to PredBB; otherwise the division is hoisted and the remainder can be decomposed into mul/sub using that division.

The tests verify that udiv and urem are hoisted to entry for i64 cases and that the i128 remainder becomes mul/sub using the hoisted division, with freeze operations added to preserve poison semantics.

assertion_or_trace: Instruction does not dominate all uses
reproducer: The issue is an -O1 optimizer-produced invalid-IR failure detected by the verifier.
This pass performs the exact high-risk operation for such a failure: moving SSA-producing instructions across basic blocks and then introducing or retaining uses of those values.
The new regression cases are triangular CFGs in which div/rem values are moved from branch-specific blocks into their common predecessor.

If an operand is defined only in one of the original blocks, moving the operation to PredBB would immediately create a non-dominating operand use and trigger the reported verifier diagnostic. build_risk: The core implementation hunk and focused transform tests were retrieved; only 5 hunks were omitted.

The pass requests and preserves CFG analyses while moving instructions without changing CFG edges, which is consistent with the shown transformation but makes SSA/dominance preconditions especially important.
Regression tests check expected transformed IR, including negative may-throw coverage in visible context, but do not explicitly run the verifier or the reported clang -O1 testcase.

Summary: This commit changes IndVarSimplify's widening eligibility so that WidenIV::getWideRecurrence only considers integer narrow uses, rather than all ScalarEvolution-supported types. In practice, this excludes pointer-typed uses from the widening path; the accompanying signed-trip-count test also changes its data layout to explicitly define 32-bit pointers.

Behavioral change: Replaces the general ScalarEvolution eligibility check, SE->isSCEVable(DU.NarrowUse->getType()), with an integer-type requirement.; Prevents WidenIV recurrence widening from applying to pointer-typed narrow uses.; Adjusts the related test data layout to make the pointer width explicit.

top_candidates.subject: [RS4GC] Use one DVCache for both inlineGetBaseAndOffset() and insertParsePoints()
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This RewriteStatepointsForGC change creates one DefiningValueMapTy cache per rewritten function and passes it to both inlineGetBaseAndOffset and insertParsePoints. Previously each phase used a separate cache. The intended result is to reuse the same defining/base value relation across both phases and avoid generating duplicate base PHIs or selects.
Changed symbols: RewriteStatepointsForGC::runOnFunction; inlineGetBaseAndOffset; insertParsePoints; DefiningValueMapTy; findBasePointers; test_duplicate_base_generation
Behavioral change: Moves DefiningValueMapTy DVCache ownership to RewriteStatepointsForGC::runOnFunction.; Passes the same cache through inlineGetBaseAndOffset and insertParsePoints.; Removes the separate local cache previously created inside insertParsePoints.; Changes the statepoint regression expectation so gc-live uses the already-created SELECTED_BASE instead of a duplicate SELECTED_BASE1 select.
Assertion or trace link: Verifier; Instruction does not dominate all uses; FPPassManager::runOnFunction; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: -O1 compilation is the reported trigger; The retrieved regression test is GC statepoint IR, not the supplied compact C reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: RewriteStatepointsForGC; DominatorTree; GC statepoint/base-pointer rewriting; Transforms/Scalar
Causal explanation: This is the closest candidate to explicit dominance-sensitive value construction: it uses DominatorTree while computing and inserting base PHIs/selects, and the changed cache determines whether a preexisting defining value is reused. Summary: This InstCombine change introduces InstCombinerImpl::pushFreezeToPreventPoisonFromPropagating and invokes it from visitFreeze. For a one-use non-poison-producing instruction with exactly one potentially poison operand, it inserts a freeze on that operand immediately before the instruction, rewrites that operand use, and replaces uses of the original later freeze with the instruction result; accompanying tests cover legal early-freeze motion and a no-motion overflow case.

The tests cover direct hoisting of division to a dominating predecessor, expansion of a remainder into multiply/subtract for i128, and CFGs with multiple switch edges, but the retrieved hunk changes no LLVM implementation code.
Changed symbols: remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_div_edges; llvm/test/Transforms/DivRemPairs/X86/div-expanded-rem-pair.ll CHECK expectations
Behavioral change: Adds test inputs and expected IR for DivRemPairs hoisting/decomposition scenarios.; Does not change pass implementation, CFG mutation logic, dominance analysis, or verifier behavior in the retrieved hunk.

Summary: This commit adds OpenMPOpt/Attributor support for recognizing OpenMP target kernels as SPMD-compatible and rewriting eligible kernels from generic mode to SPMD mode. `AAKernelInfoFunction::changeToSPMDMode` changes the kernel execution-mode global initializer and rewrites operands of target init/deinit runtime calls after manifesting; accompanying logic records incompatible instructions, emits mode-selection remarks, and adds NVPTX OpenMP transformation tests.
Changed symbols: AAKernelInfoFunction::changeToSPMDMode; AAKernelInfoCallSite; SPMDCompatibilityTracker; NumOpenMPTargetRegionKernelsSPMD; openmp-opt
Behavioral change: For kernels whose SPMD-compatibility tracker is assumed true, changes the `<kernel>_exec_mode` global initializer from one to zero.; Rewrites `__kmpc_target_init` to set its SPMD-mode argument true and generic-state-machine argument false.; Rewrites `__kmpc_target_deinit` to set its SPMD-mode argument true.; Leaves kernels with tracked incompatible instructions in generic mode and emits analysis remarks identifying potential side-effecting instructions or calls.; Treats unknown OpenMP runtime calls as generally incompatible with SPMD execution.

Reproducer link: The commit's tests exercise OpenMP target kernels on the NVPTX triple and switch their runtime execution-mode representation.; The supplied issue reproducer is only described as compact C at -O1; the retrieved evidence does not establish that it uses OpenMP, target offloading, or NVPTX.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/OpenMPOpt.cpp; Attributor; OpenMP target-offloading kernel lowering

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: DivRemPairs' optimizeDivRem gains a new common-predecessor hoisting case. When the remainder block has one successor to the division block, a unique predecessor, only safe-to-hoist preceding instructions, and no other predecessor successors, the pass moves the division before the predecessor terminator; for native div/rem pairs it also moves the remainder, otherwise it allows the existing remainder decomposition path. Tests update triangle-shaped div/rem CFG expectations, including an i128 case where a hoisted division enables urem decomposition into mul/sub.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; DivRemPairsPass::run; DivRemPairsLegacyPass; remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges
Behavioral change: Replaces the prior unconditional refusal to handle a non-dominating div/rem pair with conditional hoisting of DivInst to a common predecessor block.; Uses IsSafeToHoist to require that instructions preceding each moved div/rem are guaranteed to transfer execution to the successor.; Requires RemBB to have DivBB as its single successor, RemBB to have a unique predecessor, and every successor of that predecessor to be either RemBB or DivBB.; Sets DivDominates after moving the division, allowing the existing optimization to retain/move a paired remainder or rewrite an expanded remainder as mul/sub.; Extends expected transformed IR so the hoisted definition is in the predecessor and can dominate uses in both former paths.
Assertion or trace link: verifier; Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found; backend-fatal-error
Reproducer link: The issue is triggered by Clang -O1 after optimization produces invalid IR.; This change alters placement of SSA-producing udiv and urem instructions across CFG edges and explicitly changes whether the pass considers the division to dominate the remainder/decomposition uses.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/DivRemPairs.cpp; DivRemPairs scalar optimizer pass; DominatorTree
Causal explanation: This is a high-relevance candidate because it introduces a new CFG-sensitive instruction-motion transformation in a scalar optimization pass. Moving DivInst and optionally RemInst to PredBB changes dominance relationships, and incorrectly satisfied CFG/safety assumptions could leave operands or uses not dominated by their definitions, matching the verifier failure class.
